Step 4 (REVIEWER) runs at the same time on the same files; do not coordinate, judge alone. E2K-25 is the one expected red test (EXPECTED_RED until step 5). SAFETY RULE R2-T (decision 0113 О2, О19): never start a program of tools/src (the team server, the engine, a team command, Pixel Office) with the real home folder as HOME; never start the team server, the engine or a team command without SAI_TEAM_HOME set to a new folder under the temporary root (this step needs none of them); never set SAI_TEAM_REAL_RUNS; never start the real `claude` program; a call that names the real home or the real Pixel Office folder goes only to a spawn that records and throws; never import a program file to read it (read it as text); a command denied by the permission check is not done another way. The released spec files smoke, picker and pixel-office may be run as the released evidence in the normal environment (0113 О2: each stand gets its private home); give the spec process SAI_TEAM_HOME = a new folder under the temporary root as well. Record before your first trial and after your last whether the folder `.sai-team` exists in the real home and the sha256 of the five files of the real Pixel Office folder (read only). Change no project file other than this handoff; no commit, push or pull. The handoff holds no absolute machine paths, no temporary paths and no names of other projects of the owner. issues.text: Outside the change (behaviour of the released kit), for ORCH and DOC-UPDATER at step 10 (step 2 issue I2; ISS-0108 addendum or a new Low defect): each Chrome start of the kit leaves one folder com.google.Chrome.XXXXXX (Chrome's singleton folder) in macOS's per-user temporary folder. Measured: the kit's close (SIGTERM to the group, then SIGKILL) leaves it in 5 of 5 starts; a graceful CDP 'Browser.close' sent first makes Chrome remove it itself (1 of 1); it ignores TMPDIR (made in the per-user temporary folder while TMPDIR named another folder), so the kit cannot route it by TMPDIR. Content: a socket of a dead process and a link to a random 20-digit number, mode 0700, owner the user, in a 0700 root, no regular file: nothing sensitive; the cost is about 11800 directories. The switch does not change it (see summary). The README paragraph 'Where files go' does not name it. Proposal: in the kit's close, send Browser.close and wait a short time before the SIGTERM/SIGKILL fallback; the leftover check of section 16 could also count new com.google.Chrome.* entries. My trials left 5 such folders (names in <scratch>/e2e107-03/notes/my-chrome-folders.txt), not removed: the task says they are not mine to remove. Also seen in the root, not made by my trials and not read: 18 folders com.google.Chrome.chrome_chrome_url_fetcher_.* (2026-11-06) and 16 hidden files .com.google.Chrome.* (0600, < 1 MB each, 2026-11-06..09); my renderers' hidden files of that name were all gone after each run (7 seen, 0 left, in t3-t6); their origin is not established; the hidden files are the only kind that could hold data, so they are named for the owner.

decisions/0113 О1 says: 'The argument also keeps the browser of the normal check away from the person's keychain.' What is shown is narrower: by Chromium's source the OSCrypt key is taken from an in-memory fake instead of the keychain whatever HOME is, and under a temporary HOME no keychain file was held open in 162 polls; but the browser process still starts the Security framework's legacy layer (its group held se_SecurityMessages in 5 of 5 polled trials, the browser process itself in t3-t6), lsof does not see a brief open, and the normal check under the person's home was not measured (R2-T; under a temporary HOME the keychain is looked up elsewhere, so a temporary-HOME trial cannot answer it). The README sentence of the change does not repeat the claim and is correct. Proposal for ORCH: read О1's sentence as 'the switch removes Chrome's request for its encryption key from the keychain (by source)', or note it as not measured. Not a FAIL: a decision text is not part of the change, and the bar is not affected.

On Linux (the GitHub runner) the switch is declared only for Apple builds in Chromium, so Chrome there does not know it; not measured here: the GitHub run of step 6 is the evidence (decisions/0113 О1). 'Without the switch Chrome does not answer its first navigation under a temporary HOME' (the README's last half) is the designer's F32 and was not repeated by me: a start without the switch takes the real keychain path by source and could read the person's keychain or show a dialog on the person's screen.

A trap of trial nets, for docs/anti-patterns.md (Q13, DOC-UPDATER from result.issues): a preload that replaces child_process.execFile with a plain wrapper loses util.promisify.custom, so promisify(execFile) then resolves with the stdout string only; my first trial's poller read every answer as undefined and recorded 0 polls while the trial looked green. It was seen in the report (polls 0) and not used as evidence; the sketch was changed to a hand-made promise that still goes through the net. Copying the original's promisify.custom onto the wrapper would bypass the net, so a net should either refuse promisify use or the sketch must not use it.
